definition: Drawing of how a network is actually built, showing the real devices, cable runs and grades, WAN links, and where each piece of equipment sits.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Drawing of how data flows through a network, showing subnets, VLANs, protocols, domains, and server roles rather than hardware placement and cable paths.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Drawing of one equipment cabinet that shows which device occupies each rack unit, how the gear is mounted, and any unusual setups in it.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Documentation that traces each cable run end to end, with its type, label, and the switch, patch panel, or server port it connects to.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Drawing limited to the physical layer: the hardware, transmission media, and physical links between devices, without any addressing details.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: Drawing of data link connectivity that shows which devices can reach each other inside a LAN through switches, often with VLANs and MAC addresses.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: Drawing of routing that shows IP address spaces, the subnets in each LAN, and the routers that connect the network segments.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: Study of a building in which technicians measure signal strength, coverage gaps, dead zones, and interference to plan where access points should go.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Color-shaded floor plan of Wi-Fi signal strength, with warm colors such as red marking strong coverage and cool colors such as blue marking weak areas.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Up-to-date record of every hardware device and software title the organization owns, with models, serial numbers, versions, locations, licenses, and warranty details.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Tracking of the legal rights to use each software product, such as how many users or devices are allowed and when the agreement must be renewed.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: Vendor coverage that repairs or replaces failed hardware at no extra cost for a set period after purchase, recorded with each device in the inventory.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Planning, tracking, and monitoring of a network's address space, including ranges, subnets, reservations, and which host holds each address, often with a dedicated tool.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Contract with a provider that states measurable service terms, such as 99.999 percent uptime and repair times, and what happens if they are missed.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Oversight of a system from planning and deployment through maintenance and upgrades to its final retirement, so aging parts are replaced in time.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: Stage at which the manufacturer stops making, selling, and marketing a product; support and warranty coverage may also be ending.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Date after which the vendor no longer supplies security fixes, software updates, or technical help for a product, leaving devices still in use exposed.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Small vendor-supplied code update that corrects a bug or closes a security hole in an operating system or application without replacing the whole program.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: Process of watching for new vendor fixes, testing them on lab systems, and deploying them across the network's devices, often with automated tools.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Glossary; checked against CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: Replacement of the low-level code embedded in hardware such as a router or switch, to fix bugs, close security holes, or add features.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Planned retirement of a device, application, or service: dependencies are checked, data is backed up or migrated, and the system is removed from production.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: Return to the previous software version or saved settings when a patch, upgrade, or change causes problems.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Glossary; checked against CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: Formal process for requesting, reviewing, approving, scheduling, and documenting changes to the network, so each change has a reason, a back-out plan, and approval.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Official logged ticket asking for a change or service, tracked from submission through approval and completion, listing the impact and back-out steps.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Approved, scheduled period of downtime, usually outside business hours, during which changes to production systems are carried out.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Glossary; checked against CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: Ongoing process of documenting device settings, keeping them in a desired state, and tracking every settings change over time with versions and audits.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: The live settings a device runs with in service, tested and validated for performance, security, and function before deployment.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Saved snapshot of a device's live settings from a point in time, kept so the device can be restored quickly after a failure or a bad change.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Tested, approved standard set of settings that similar devices are compared against to find and correct any differences.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Unsolicited alert that an agent on a managed device sends to the manager when a set condition occurs, such as a failed interface, normally to UDP port 162.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: Hierarchical database that lists every object SNMP can read or set on a managed device, each object named by a numeric identifier.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Dotted string of numbers that uniquely names one managed item, such as a CPU load counter, within the SNMP database tree.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: SNMP release still widely used that improved performance but authenticates only with plaintext community strings and sends data without encryption.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: Most secure SNMP release, adding user-based authentication, message integrity checks, and encryption such as AES instead of plaintext community strings.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: Plaintext password-like value that SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c devices check before they answer requests; it can grant read-only or read-write access.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Central console software that gathers data from managed devices, receives their alerts, and shows maps and graphs of device health across the network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: Small software routine on a managed device that gathers data about the device and answers manager requests, listening on UDP port 161.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: Method in which the manager asks each managed device for data at regular intervals with Get requests, instead of waiting for alerts.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: Summary records of traffic crossing router and switch interfaces, with source and destination addresses, ports, and byte counts, used to find top talkers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: Cisco protocol that keeps a record of each conversation crossing an enabled interface and exports these records to a collector for bandwidth analysis.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: Recording of complete frames, headers and payload, as they cross the network, so they can be inspected live or saved and studied later.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Switch feature that copies the traffic of one or more ports or VLANs to a chosen port where a monitoring tool or analyzer is connected.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Record of normal network performance, such as utilization, error rate, and latency, taken over time and used as a point of comparison.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: Automatic warning sent when a monitored value strays from its normal level or crosses a threshold, such as a sudden spike in traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Gathering of log data from many devices and applications into one central store so it can be searched, correlated, and analyzed together.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Full handling of system-generated event records over their life, including collection, retention, review, and secure disposal.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Central server that listens for event messages from network devices, usually on UDP port 514, and stores them with their severity levels.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Platform that gathers logs from firewalls, servers, and IDS sensors, correlates events in real time, and alerts staff to likely threats on a dashboard.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Analysis that links related entries from different devices' logs to reveal attack patterns that no single entry would show.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Linking monitoring tools to ticketing, orchestration, or configuration systems through programmable interfaces, so alerts can open tickets or start fixes automatically.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Scanning that finds and catalogs the hosts, devices, and services on a network, with their addresses and operating systems, to build an inventory.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: On-demand scan an administrator runs, such as a ping sweep of one segment, in response to a specific problem or question.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Automated scan that repeats at set intervals to keep the asset inventory and topology map current and to detect new or changed devices.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Study of packet flow patterns across the network to find congestion points, bottlenecks, heavy users, and unusual behavior.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Tracking of measures such as bandwidth, latency, jitter, CPU, and memory use on devices and links to spot slowdowns before users notice them.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Constant checking that devices, servers, and services are reachable and running, so outages and downtime are detected and fixed quickly.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Ongoing comparison of device settings with an approved standard to catch unauthorized changes and drift and to verify compliance with policy.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Encrypted tunnel between gateways at two or more locations, such as a branch and headquarters, so whole networks connect securely over the Internet.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Encrypted tunnel from one remote user's device, usually running client software, to a gateway at the edge of the corporate network.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Remote access through a web browser to a secure portal protected by SSL/TLS, with no dedicated tunneling software installed on the device.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: Remote access setup in which only traffic for the corporate network uses the encrypted tunnel, while Internet traffic goes out directly through the local connection.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: Remote access setup that sends all of a client's traffic, including Internet browsing, through the encrypted tunnel to the corporate network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: Direct local access to a device through its dedicated serial management port and cable, used for initial setup, password recovery, and when the network is down.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Management method that uses windows, menus, icons, and a pointer, often a web page, instead of typed commands.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Programmatic way for scripts and software to send requests to a device and receive structured responses, used to automate configuration and management.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Hardened server that administrators must log in to first, with strong authentication and logging, before they can reach protected internal systems.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Device administration over the same network paths that carry user traffic, such as SSH or a web page, so it is lost when that network fails.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: Device administration over a separate dedicated path, such as a console server, modem, or management network, that still works when the production network fails.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: A disaster recovery metric for the most data loss a business can accept, measured back in time to the last usable backup or copy.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: A disaster recovery metric for the longest outage a service may have before the downtime harms the business, which sets how fast systems must be restored.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: The average time needed to fix a failed device or system and put it back in service; a lower value means faster recovery.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: The average time a device or system runs normally before it breaks down, used to predict reliability; a higher value means fewer outages.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: A disaster recovery location with space, power, and basic connectivity but little or no ready equipment, so restoring service takes days or longer; the cheapest option.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: A disaster recovery location with equipment in place but only partly configured or updated, so data restores and setup take hours to days; mid-range cost.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: A disaster recovery location fully equipped, configured, and kept current with production, so operations can move there almost at once; the most expensive option.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: A disaster recovery option hosted by a provider, where cloud resources are kept running or built by scripts only when a disaster strikes.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: A high-availability design in which all redundant devices or links carry traffic at the same time and share the load, so any one can absorb a failure.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking

definition: A high-availability design in which one device or link carries all traffic while a standby copy stays idle and takes over only after a failure.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking

definition: The automatic switch of work from a failed component to a redundant one, so the service keeps running with little or no interruption.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Glossary; checked against CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation

definition: One device, link, or service whose loss stops a whole network or process because nothing redundant can take its place.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: A disaster recovery test in which team members meet and talk through a pretend disaster to check roles, decisions, and communication, without running any recovery steps.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: A hands-on disaster recovery test that actually runs restore and failover procedures in a controlled setting to prove they work and meet time and data-loss targets.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

definition: The part of continuity planning that documents the contacts, backups, and steps used to restore critical systems and data after a major outage.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: A high-level plan for keeping an organization serving its customers during and after a disaster, covering critical operations, communications, and ways to limit downtime.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery

definition: The range of IPv4 addresses, with its subnet settings, that a DHCP server may hand out to clients on one network segment.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A setting that makes the DHCP server always give the same IP address to one client, identified by its MAC address, such as a network printer.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: How long a client may keep an address from a DHCP server; the client tries to renew at about half that period and stops using the address when it expires.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: Extra settings a DHCP server sends along with each address, such as the default gateway, DNS servers, domain suffix, and how long the address is valid.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: Addresses inside a DHCP address range that the server never hands out, kept free for devices that use static IP addresses.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A router or layer 3 switch that picks up DHCP broadcasts on a local subnet and forwards them to a DHCP server on another subnet.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: The address set on a router interface to forward selected UDP broadcasts, by default DHCP, DNS, TFTP, and more, to a server or subnet elsewhere.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation

definition: The first message of the address assignment process, a broadcast from a client with no IP address that looks for any available DHCP server.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: The second message of the address assignment process, in which a DHCP server proposes an available address, its duration, and settings to the client.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: The third message of the address assignment process, in which the client tells the chosen DHCP server that it accepts the proposed address.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: The fourth and final message of the address assignment process, in which the DHCP server confirms the assignment so the client can start using the address.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: An IPv6 method in which a host builds its own address from the network prefix that routers announce plus an interface ID, without a DHCPv6 server.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: The IPv6 check in which a host tests whether another node already uses its new address before the host starts using that address.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: An IPv6 message that a host sends to ask local routers for configuration information such as the network prefix.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: An IPv6 message sent by a router that gives hosts the network prefix and other settings they use to configure their own addresses.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A DNS resource record that maps a hostname to a 32-bit IPv4 address, used for forward lookups.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: A DNS resource record that maps a hostname to a 128-bit IPv6 address, used for forward lookups on IPv6 networks.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: A DNS resource record that makes one hostname an alias of another, so several names lead to the same host.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A DNS resource record that names the email servers that receive mail for a domain, with a preference number for each server.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A DNS resource record that holds free-form text, often used for SPF and DKIM email checks and to prove domain ownership.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A DNS resource record that lists the authoritative DNS servers for a domain, often used to delegate a subdomain to other servers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A DNS resource record that maps an IP address back to a hostname, stored with the address octets reversed under the in-addr.arpa domain.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: The first DNS resource record in a zone file, holding the contact address, serial number, and refresh timers that control zone transfers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: The part of a DNS database that answers a hostname query with an IP address, mainly through A and AAAA records; the most common type.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: The part of a DNS database that answers an IP address query with a hostname, using PTR records under the in-addr.arpa domain.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: The portion of the DNS namespace, made of one or more domains, that one organization manages and that its name servers hold records for.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Glossary; checked against CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: The copying of DNS records from the main authoritative server to a backup authoritative server so that both hold the same data.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: The main authoritative server for a zone, holding the editable master copy of its records that backup servers copy from.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A backup authoritative server that holds a read-only copy of a zone and gets updates by requesting them from the main server.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A DNS query that requires the server to return the final answer or an error, so the server queries other servers itself if needed.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A DNS query in which the server replies only with what it already knows, often a referral to another server, and the asker continues the search.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A DNS reply that comes straight from a name server that holds the zone file for the domain, such as its primary or secondary server.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: A DNS reply taken from a cache or learned from other servers, given by a server that does not hold the zone for that domain.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: A DNS server that holds no zone files of its own and resolves queries for local clients, keeping each answer until its time to live ends.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A local text file that maps hostnames to IP addresses by hand, used for name resolution on a few hosts or to block unwanted sites.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: Additions to DNS that use digital signatures and public keys so that resolvers can check that records are authentic and were not changed.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: A method that encrypts DNS queries inside normal web traffic on TCP port 443, usually set in the browser, which hides lookups among other traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: A method that encrypts DNS queries directly with Transport Layer Security on its own port, 853, so secure DNS traffic is easy to identify and manage.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: A DNS feature that lets hosts register and update their own name-to-address records automatically when addresses change, instead of manual edits.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: A DNS setup that gives internal and external clients different answers for the same name, for example a private address inside and a public one outside.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: An IEEE 1588 protocol that uses hardware timestamps and one main clock to sync devices far more accurately than NTP, used in telecom, trading, and industry.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

definition: A security addition, defined in RFC 8915, that uses TLS and cryptographic checks to protect NTP and PTP time traffic against spoofing and tampering.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: The level number of a time server in the NTP hierarchy, counting hops from the reference clock at 0; each hop adds one, up to 16.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

definition: In PTP, the one main clock chosen to lead timing for the whole network, which sends sync messages that all other clocks follow.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
